checks: No eclipse at 16 of 229 covered epochs where the 1.99834 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.
writeup: TIC 237226943 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 1.9983 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse produces a 1.02% dimming signal with a detection significance of 168.5 in the BLS periodogram, while no secondary eclipse was detected. Pixel-level analysis yielded a difference-imaging signal-to-noise of 39.2, though the centroid offset of 1.0 arcsec from the target raises an important consideration: TESS's resolution cannot confidently separate this star from a nearby bright neighbor, with the centroid separation of only 0.051 pixels falling within the instrument's stated systematic uncertainty. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, and the pipeline's machine-learning model assigns it a 0.62 screening score. Further observations would be needed to definitively confirm whether the signal originates from the target star itself.
